title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease, with right to cure
requirement: When a tenant under a written lease fails to pay rent due, the landlord must give a written 14-day notice to quit to end the lease. The lease is not ended if the tenant pays or tenders all rent due, with interest and costs of suit, on or before the day the answer is due in the landlord's possession action. This section sets notice and cure rules for nonpayment; it does not create a general just-cause requirement.
key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit
coverage_conditions: Tenancies under a written lease where the tenant has neglected or refused to pay rent due.
quoted_span: Section 11. Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

x_details.text: If nonpayment was caused by a government failure or delay in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days. If all rent due with interest and costs is tendered within that time, the court treats the tenancy as not terminated.

x_plain: If you have a written lease and fall behind on rent, your landlord must give you 14 days' written notice to end it, but you can keep your home by paying all rent owed plus interest and court costs by the day your answer is due in court.

title: Notice to terminate a tenancy at will (including 14-day notice for nonpayment and right to cure)
requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice equal to the longer of the rent payment interval or 30 days (three months if rent is paid less often). x_details.text: For nonpayment of rent, a 14-day written notice to quit is sufficient, but a tenant with no similar notice in the prior 12 months can prevent termination by paying the full rent due within 10 days of receiving the notice.

x_details.quoted_span: If any notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall fail to contain such notification, the time within which the tenant receiving the notice would be entitled to pay or tender rent pursuant to this section shall be extended to the day the answer is due in any action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises.

x_details.text: If nonpayment was caused by a government delay in a subsistence or rental payment or voucher, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days and treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent with interest and costs is tendered.
x_details.quoted_span: If the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due was caused by a failure or delay of the federal government, the commonwealth or any municipality, or any departments, agencies or authorities thereof, in the mailing or delivery of any subsistence or rental payment, check or voucher other than a salary payment to either the tenant or the landlord, the court in any action for possession shall continue the hearing not less than seven days in order to furnish notice of such action to the appropriate agency and shall, if all rent due with interest and costs of suit has been tendered to the landlord within such time, treat the tenancy as not having been terminated.

x_plain: If you rent month to month, your landlord must give you written notice of at least one rental period or 30 days (whichever is longer) to end your tenancy, and if the notice is for unpaid rent you get 14 days' notice and can usually stop the eviction by paying all rent owed within 10 days.
